source.title: Controllable Context Sensitivity and the Knob Behind It
source.authors: Julian Minder; Kevin Du; Niklas Stoehr; Giovanni Monea; C. Wendler; Robert West; Ryan Cotterell

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies a rank-1 subspace for controlling whether language models use context or prior knowledge, not sparse-feature superposition, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, or SAE feature completeness.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for controllable context sensitivity and steering a context-versus-prior subspace. These are related representation findings, but do not test whether sparse features overlap in limited dimensions. Its subspace results are recorded under fits_no_version; no result tests V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The study learns a rank-1 subspace (via distributed alignment search) for a context-versus-prior intent variable in Llama-3.1, Gemma-2 and Mistral, and reports steering PairAcc. It does not study sparse features, feature count versus dimension, polysemantic neurons, capacity, SAEs, or whether superposed features are 1-D rather than multi-dimensional. The rank-1 choice is assumed from the linear subspace hypothesis, not tested against higher-rank alternatives. Superposition is not discussed at all, so 'cites_only' or T6 fits better than 'discusses'; T6 is kept.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude a 1-D subspace in a single layer encodes whether the model follows context or prior knowledge. They find it transfers across fine-tuned, instruct and base models within a family, and similar subspaces are found in Gemma-2 and Mistral. They note it works best when the answer can be copied directly from context.
record.recipe_differences: The study learns and intervenes on a rank-1 context-versus-prior subspace; it does not apply the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Context-control performance varies with model configuration, dataset, and intent formulation. The paper reports weaker generalization for some out-of-domain datasets and intent formats.

fits_no_version.finding: A rank-1 subspace at layer 16 of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct FT steers context-vs-prior answering without an intent instruction: 83% PairAcc vs 95% instruction baseline. It transfers to non-fine-tuned instruct and base models of the same family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single learned direction in one layer can act as a knob between answering from context and from prior knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: Separation of ctx and pri intents along the subspace correlates with PairAcc across configurations: 0.908 Llama, 0.871 Mistral, 0.975 Gemma.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models better at controllable context sensitivity separate the two intents more distinctly in the identified subspace.

record.problems: The reported results concern a constructed context-sensitivity task, not superposition. The authors note that performance is better when the context directly states the answer and that use of context in intermediate reasoning needs further investigation. The main subspace is learned using examples the model answered correctly for both intents, and steering constants are selected on a validation set.
record.rows_left_out: Other context-sensitivity and steering results, including additional model families and datasets, were not extracted because they do not test any listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: toy models, sparsity, feature overlap, phase transition, geometry.
All: capacity competition, dedicated vs shared dimensions.
All: distribution of features across neurons, dictionary/SAE recovery.
All: completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
Whether superposed features are 1-D. Rank-1 is assumed, and no higher-rank comparison is reported.

record.verdict_notes: No result bears on any superposition version. The Gemma and Mistral correlations (App. H) are reasonably left out under rows_left_out, since they too fit no version. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because the paper never engages superposition; it only invokes the linear subspace hypothesis.

versions.untested_parts: Does not study sparse features, feature count versus dimensionality, overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or recoverable with a dictionary or SAE.
Does not assess whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Finds a one-dimensional subspace for a context-versus-prior decision, but does not test whether features involved in superposition are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (INSTR FT)
rows.operation_detail: At layer 16, replace the rank-1 subspace component with a manually set value and evaluate without an explicit intent instruction.
rows.note: The paper reports this as evidence that a rank-1 subspace can control context-versus-prior behavior. It does not measure superposition or sparse-feature geometry.
rows.check: Steering accuracy of a learned rank-1 subspace on a task. It measures no superposition, polysemanticity or SAE-feature property. The link is correct; the value and baseline (83% vs 95%, Fig. 3) match the text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1 model configurations
rows.operation_detail: Correlate PairAcc with the difference in subspace values between context and prior intents.

conditions.value: multiple fine-tuned, in-context-learning, and zero-shot configurations

rows.measure: Pearson correlation between subspace-value mean difference and PairAcc
rows.note: Reported as a correlation across model configurations; it concerns context-control performance, not sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: Correlation across 12 Llama configurations between subspace mean difference and PairAcc (0.908, Fig. 5). It does not bear on any version. Subject should read 'Llama-3.1-8B base and instruct across ZS/ICL/FT and two intent formats'.
